PullRequest.Title: chat: truncate response stats that do not fit after the progress label
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #349171.

With the response stats shown after the working progress label (`chat.responseStats` set to `progressWithMessage`, its default in Insiders), a narrow chat laid that row out badly in two ways:

- **A working phrase wrapped beside the stats.** The phrase gave up its width while the stats kept theirs, so "Feeding the gremlins" broke onto a second line next to "13m 14s · 21.4k tokens".
- **The stats were drawn over a background activity pill.** The pill's container shrank but the pill inside it did not, so "90m 32s · 47.1k tokens" landed on top of "1 background command running". The rule in `chat.css` that lets the pill shrink tied on specificity with the pill sizing in `chatPills.css` and lost.

Now the label or pill keeps its width, and the stats take only what is left of the row and end in an ellipsis.

## Changes

- `chat.css`: the trailing stats are the item in the row that gives way. They shrink and ellipsize, and are capped at the width of their text so their hover does not cover the empty rest of the row.
- `chat.css`: the pill's shrink rule names both of the widget's classes, so it outranks `chatPills.css` whatever the stylesheet order.
- `chatListRenderer.test.ts`: a layout test for a label and for a pill, each at three row widths.

## Behavior to know about

- A row narrower than the label itself still wraps the label, as it does with the stats off. A pill ellipsizes instead.
- When the stats are clipped away entirely next to a pill, the "·" separator before them stays visible.
- The `progress` placement (stats before the label) is unchanged: a label that names a state can still wrap beside the stats there.

## How to test

1. Set `chat.responseStats` to `progressWithMessage`.
2. Start a response that runs for a while, then narrow the chat until the stats no longer fit after the working phrase. The phrase stays on one line and the stats end in "…".
3. Do the same while a background command is running, so the row reads "1 background command running". The stats shorten and never overlap it.

## Validation

- Passed, 1129 passing and 2 pending:
  ```
  ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatLiveResponseStats.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/chatPills.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widgetHosts/viewPane/chatViewTitleControl.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatTurnPills.test.ts --reporter dot
  ```
- Passed: `pnpm run typecheck-client`
- Passed: `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/media/chat.css src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts`
- The new test fails on the previous CSS, and fails again with either of the two CSS changes reverted.
- Not run locally: the component fixture screenshot check. Measured in the unit test environment, a row wide enough for its stats lays out identically with and without the new stats rule.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display and resize a running response's progress label with trailing stats
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The browser lays out and paints the existing progress row after width, label, or stats changes. The diff changes flex sizing and clipping; it adds no asynchronous prerequisite to response delivery or input.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser flex layout and text ellipsis for the existing trailing stats span
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One affected span per rendered working footer; normal layout invalidations follow existing resize and text-update frequency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same span was laid out on the same events but retained its width, allowing the adjacent label to wrap. The new rules change the distribution of available width.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Normal layout and paint remain on the UI rendering path; no new JavaScript layout loop is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Rendered running-response footers, resize events, existing progress-label updates, and existing approximately once-per-second stats updates. Each affected footer contains one trailing stats span with a short numeric summary, not response-length text.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser UI work is synchronous. Existing stats schedulers and progress updates are unchanged; no new parallel requests or queued work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache changes. Clean browser layout is reused until existing width or content updates invalidate it; max-content sizing operates on the short stats string.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete CSS diff, stats updater, footer construction, and narrow-row test. No changed mechanism establishes increased scaling or repeated work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser layout duration and the number of simultaneously rendered chats are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: CSS changes sizing of existing elements without adding nodes, events, or boundary calls. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is added or moved onto this path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display and resize background-activity pills beside trailing response stats
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing activity observables select the visible pill, then the browser sizes its label and trailing stats. Narrow-row rendering does not wait for command execution or retrieval of additional activity details.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser sizing and clipping of the existing dropdown pill
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One visible summary pill per activity footer, including when multiple entries or both activity sources exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same pill and activity sections existed; a competing 280px maximum-width rule outranked or tied the intended percentage-width rule. There were no additional per-entry operations during resizing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Ordinary row layout; the selector correction allows the pill to shrink instead of overflowing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Activity entries feed existing section observables, but the footer uses one visible summary pill: subagents, background shells, or a combined summary. Three candidate pill definitions are pre-existing, not one new boundary call per entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing observable updates and browser layout run on the UI thread. CSS does not issue or synchronize background commands, and existing pill entry actions remain outside the sizing path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Activity sources and derived section subscriptions are unchanged. The selector introduces no fetching, caching, or negative-cache behavior; browser layout can reuse clean geometry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the footer's source/combined pill selection and both competing stylesheets.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Activity-list sizes and browser layout cost are unmeasured, but those sizes do not multiply newly introduced external operations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: the specificity change restores intended shrink behavior. It does not change activity acquisition, pill construction frequency, entry-action execution, or subprocess/IPC/filesystem/database/network boundaries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover live response stats in trailing progress, leading progress, or the chat title
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On mouseover, the hover service resolves the existing options callback synchronously, then constructs and schedules the existing hover. The diff reads truncation geometry before returning a short plain-text hover string.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read scrollWidth and clientWidth to detect clipping
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pair of reads per hover-options evaluation, not per streaming update, timer tick, resize event, or mousemove.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The options callback returned explanatory text without geometry reads; invocation frequency and hover scheduling were the same.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: May synchronously flush dirty layout on mouseover, before the existing hover delay. There is no read/write loop or collection-scale invocation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and render the existing plain-text hover content
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One short hover per requested target, governed by the existing current-hover identity and disposal logic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same plain-string rendering branch displayed only explanatory text. Hover creation frequency and ownership are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing hover construction/display path; truncated stats add a short numeric line, not markdown rendering or remote content resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two geometry reads for the single target per mouseover or explicit hover invocation. The span contains only time and token count/speed; no child-element mouseover fan-out, history scan, or response-text serialization is introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Callback and geometry reads are synchronous on the UI thread. Hover display uses the existing configured delay; no per-frame evaluation or concurrent boundary burst is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Clean browser layout satisfies geometry reads without a dirty-layout flush. Existing current/delayed hover identity handling remains; text is evaluated on demand and not cached across growing response histories.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the two reads are newly introduced and mouseover-bound, corroborated by hover-service implementation and its options-evaluation test. Insufficient evidence of a concrete user-visible performance regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A dirty-layout flush could vary with the surrounding workbench, but no evidence establishes a realistically frequent or scaling regression from this bounded hover-only check.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: a bounded on-demand truncation check and short string addition do not establish hot-path amplification. The plain-string branch adds no network, filesystem, database, IPC, subprocess, markdown, or dynamic-content observer work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start, finish, or relocate response stats between progress and title
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing configuration/model observables select the active stats location and update its span. Starting a response does not evaluate the new hover callback; response completion hides stats and releases existing scheduler state through observable ownership.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing title instance and two progress-placement instances per relevant host/footer. Only the configured location of an incomplete response reads usage and schedules updates; hidden placements remain inactive.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing RunOnceScheduler updates occur approximately once per second while running and stop rescheduling during confirmation waits. All instances retain their existing disposal ownership; the diff adds no scheduler or concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing observable configuration reads, derived visibility gating, and module-level numeric formatters are unchanged. No new response retention, cache key, failure retry, or eagerly resolved hover content.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete stats implementation and title/footer callers: only the hover callback body and CSS change in production.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Number of concurrently open chat hosts and rate of usage events are unmeasured, but the diff does not change either cost multiplier.
Scenarios.Verdict: No startup, streaming, or lifetime regression. Constructor work, timer frequency, inactive-instance gating, disposal, and external boundary counts are unchanged; no new expensive external call is on this path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all four changed files and all diff pages against base 76c524d086fddfaebe4ce07d41d82b964365fd1a. Traced CSS layout, summary-pill grouping, all stats hosts, hover callback frequency and plain-text rendering, scheduler gating, and disposal ownership. No high-confidence introduced performance regression or concrete historical performance-regression fix qualifies. Static review; browser timing was not measured.
